title: Why does the impossible triangle look possible?
description: A triangle of three bars seems to close, though every corner is a right angle bend. The board shows that it cannot be built from real cubes, draws the bars as rows of cubes on the grid, and explains the illusion by the depth that a drawing loses.
teaching_notes: One idea: a flat drawing loses depth, so a near end and a far end can land on the same point and look joined. Watch for students who think a drawing that looks right must be possible to build.

video_script.why: The child decides that the impossible triangle cannot be built and explains the illusion by the depth that a drawing loses.
video_script.substitution: Test each corner in real space, then ask which ends only look joined because a drawing loses depth.
video_script.anchor: a triangle of three bars of cubes, each joined to the next by a right angle bend, drawn on a grid
video_script.payoff_line: The illusion works because the projection loses depth, so far and near ends appear to touch

final_answer.value: It cannot be built; the illusion works because the projection loses depth, so far and near ends appear to touch
final_answer.spoken: it cannot be built; the illusion works because the projection loses depth, so far and near ends appear to touch

hold_back: Answer: It cannot be built; the illusion works because the projection loses depth, so far and near ends appear to touch
never_show: a real model of the triangle marked as possible
maths_rules: each corner looks like a right angle bend, but three such bends cannot close into a triangle in real space
a real model of rows of cubes looks right only from one viewpoint
a projection loses depth: a near end and a far end can land on the same point
video_script.design: The triangle of three bars on the stage. A side view pulls the bars apart in depth to show the gap, then the grid drawing joins the near end and the far end on one point.
open_questions: The impossible triangle of the book is a picture that is not in the extracted text, so the video works from the worklist steps. The front, top and side profiles of part (i) are not drawn out, since they need the picture.
